definitions.gloss: washing rice; rinsing rice before cooking
definitions.explanation: The process of rinsing raw rice with water to remove starch and impurities before cooking. A fundamental step in preparing Japanese rice.

examples.japanese: {炊飯|すいはん}の{前|まえ}に{洗米|せんまい}する。
examples.english: To wash the rice before cooking.

examples.japanese: {洗米|せんまい}は{水|みず}が{透明|とうめい}になるまで{繰|く}り{返|かえ}す。
examples.english: Repeat the rice washing until the water becomes clear.

examples.japanese: {無洗米|むせんまい}なら{洗米|せんまい}の{手間|てま}が{省|はぶ}けて{便利|べんり}だ。
examples.english: No-wash rice is convenient because it saves you the trouble of washing.

notes:
Composed of {洗|せん} (wash) + {米|まい} (rice). Refers specifically to the rinsing of uncooked rice. The everyday expression is {米|こめ}を{研|と}ぐ or {米|こめ}を{洗|あら}う, while {洗米|せんまい} is the more formal or technical term.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {洗米|せんまい}する (to wash rice)
- {洗米|せんまい}の{回数|かいすう} (number of rice-washing rinses)
- {無洗米|むせんまい} (no-wash rice, pre-rinsed rice)
- {洗米|せんまい}{後|ご}に{水|みず}に{浸|ひた}す (to soak in water after washing)

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {米|こめ}を{研|と}ぐ — to wash/polish rice; the everyday kitchen expression
- {無洗米|むせんまい} — no-wash rice; rice that has been pre-processed to remove the bran layer
- {炊飯|すいはん} — rice cooking; the step that follows {洗米|せんまい}

USAGE:
{洗米|せんまい} appears on rice packaging instructions, in recipe books, and in food industry contexts. In casual conversation, {米|こめ}を{研|と}ぐ is more natural. {無洗米|むせんまい} (no-wash rice) has become popular for its convenience and water-saving benefits.
